questions.prompt: Why does the Moon usually look different from night to night?
options: Clouds always hide half of it
We see different amounts of its sunlit half
It makes more of its own light
questions.explanation: The Moon stays round. Its journey around Earth changes our view of its bright side.

options: The bright part we see is getting bigger
questions.explanation: Waxing describes a growing bright part as seen from Earth, not a change in the Moon’s size.

questions.prompt: At first quarter, how much of the Moon’s face looks bright?
questions.explanation: The word quarter refers to progress through the cycle. About half of the face looks bright.

title: Why does the Moon seem to change shape?
practice: Explore more astronomy and everyday science in Science Quiz.

sections.html:
A crescent Moon looks like a thin smile. A full Moon looks like a bright circle. But the Moon has not grown a new piece or lost a bite.

The Moon stays round. It looks different because we see different amounts of its bright side.

The Moon does not make its own light like the Sun. Sunlight falls on it, and some of that light reaches our eyes.
sections.title: The Moon stays round

sections.html:
Hold a ball near a lamp. The side facing the lamp is bright; the other side is dark.

The Sun lights the Moon in a similar way: roughly half is sunlit. As the Moon travels around Earth, our view of that bright half changes.

Sometimes we see a lot of it. Sometimes we see only a thin slice. We call those different views the Moon’s phases.
sections.title: Picture a ball beside a lamp

sections.html:
Waxing means the bright part we see is getting bigger from night to night. Waning means it is getting smaller. The Moon itself is not growing or shrinking.

First quarter is a trickier name. At that stage, about half of the Moon’s face looks bright. “Quarter” means it is about a quarter of the way through its cycle of phases—not that only a quarter looks lit.
sections.title: Three names that can sound confusing

sections.html:
Different views of the same Moon
NameWhat its face looks like from Earth
New MoonAlmost none of the bright half faces us
First quarterAbout half of the face looks bright
Full MoonAlmost all of the face looks bright
sections.title: What can we see?

sections.html:
Usually, no. The ordinary phases come from our changing view of the sunlit half.

Sometimes Earth does cast its shadow on the Moon. That special event is a lunar eclipse. It is different from the normal monthly phases.
sections.title: Is Earth’s shadow covering it?

sections.html:
When you can see the Moon, draw its bright shape and write down the time. Look again on another clear evening.

Is the bright part bigger or smaller? You do not need to remember every phase name to start spotting the pattern.

The Moon may be in a different place or may not be visible at your chosen time. That is fine: look again another day.
sections.title: Try noticing it for yourself

description: One night it looks like a thin smile; another night it is a bright circle. The Moon stays round. What changes is how much of its sunlit side we can see.
